svg.title: Copper Scroll entry 1: the ruin in the Valley of Achor
svg.text: Entry 1 (I 1–4) — the ruin in the Valley of Achor
Schematic plan, north up. One arrangement the text allows; the ruin's shape and the valley's course are not given and are drawn generic.
Project reading: forty cubits along the line of the steps
The steps go in toward the east; the deposit lies under their line, 40 cubits from them.
The text names no starting point for the 40 cubits; here it is the inner end of the steps.
the valley floor; its course is not given
chest of silver and its vessels
buried under the line of the steps
1 cubit taken as about 0.5 m; ruin size generic, drawn to hold the 40 cubits
The files leave distance against depth open.
Section, east to the right, depth compressed.
The word after “cubits” is disputed; the plan only stretches.
Pixner and García Martínez–Tigchelaar read “go past”,
which removes the Valley of Achor.
Only the ruin and its steps
Readings that leave the plan unchanged
a chest (Puech) or a carrying chair (Lefkovits).
“little ruin”, Ḥorebbeh, with yod (Milik, Puech); with
Wadi Nuweiʿimeh (Milik, Puech) or the Buqeia (Allegro,
“In the ruin that is in the Valley of Achor, under the steps that go in toward the east, forty
cubits: a chest of silver and its vessels, weighing seventeen talents. ΚΕΝ”
Forty cubits is a distance along the line of the steps (phase 1 treats it as a distance); the start
point is not stated. The ruin is drawn large enough to hold it.
Atlas: best-supported, low. Wadi Nuweiʿimeh NE of Jericho preferred (low); the Buqeia plateau and the
Ruins of several periods and undated channels are reported in the valley, but none with steps or a
ruin that can be named Ḥorebbeh; it stays at valley level (phase5_assessments.csv).
